_comment: Multi-dialect SQL DDL conversion rules. Supports MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL, IBM DB2, SAP HANA, Snowflake as source and/or target dialects. Each mapping specifies how a type/function is handled per dialect pair.

metadata.description: Rules-driven conversion engine supporting multiple SQL dialects

type_mappings._comment: key = common base type (uppercase, dialect-agnostic). target = {dialect: {target_type, carry_args, fixed_args, review}}

tsql.review: SQL Server TINYINT is unsigned 0-255; other databases have no exact equivalent. Choose appropriate target type and add range CHECK if needed.

oracle.review: Oracle has no TINYINT; mapped to NUMBER(3,0).

postgresql.review: PostgreSQL has no TINYINT; mapped to SMALLINT.

db2.review: DB2 has no TINYINT; mapped to SMALLINT.

snowflake.review: Snowflake has no unsigned types; mapped to SMALLINT.

hana->snowflake.review: SAP HANA TINYINT (0-255) mapped to Snowflake NUMBER(3,0).

oracle.review: Oracle uses NUMBER(1,0) for boolean-like values.

db2.review: DB2 uses SMALLINT for boolean values.

tsql.review: T-SQL typically uses BIT; BOOLEAN columns are rare but mapped if present.

oracle.review: Oracle does not support BOOLEAN as a column type in SQL; often represented as NUMBER(1,0) or CHAR(1).

db2.review: DB2 often models boolean as SMALLINT or CHAR(1).

mysql.review: MySQL VARCHAR is already Unicode; NVARCHAR is not a distinct type.

snowflake.review: Oracle NVARCHAR2 mapped to Snowflake VARCHAR.
SAP HANA ALPHANUM (alphanumeric text) mapped to Snowflake VARCHAR.
SAP HANA SHORTTEXT mapped to Snowflake VARCHAR.

tsql.review: TEXT is deprecated; mapped to max VARCHAR.

mysql.review: MySQL TEXT mapped to Snowflake VARCHAR

oracle.review: Oracle CLOBs have different semantics than TEXT.

mysql.review: LONGTEXT mapped to VARCHAR (may require large size).

snowflake.review: CLOB mapped to Snowflake VARCHAR (max 16MB).
NCLOB mapped to Snowflake VARCHAR (max 16MB).
DB CLOBs mapped to large VARCHAR in Snowflake; confirm size.
Map long text to large VARCHAR.

tsql.review: SQL Server uses JSON as text; map to VARIANT for semi-structured data.

snowflake.review: JSON data mapped to Snowflake semi-structured VARIANT.
BLOB mapped to Snowflake BINARY (max 8MB).
Oracle RAW binary data mapped to Snowflake BINARY.

tsql.review: IMAGE is deprecated in SQL Server.

oracle.review: Oracle DATE includes time; behavior differs from SQL Server DATETIME.

oracle->snowflake.review: Oracle DATE includes date and time components; mapped to Snowflake TIMESTAMP_NTZ to preserve time precision.

oracle.review: Oracle uses INTERVAL for time representation.

snowflake.review: SAP HANA SECONDDATE (second-precision timestamp) mapped to Snowflake TIMESTAMP_NTZ.
SAP HANA LONGDATE (nanosecond-precision timestamp) mapped to Snowflake TIMESTAMP_NTZ.
Preserve timezone information in Snowflake TIMESTAMP_TZ.
Oracle TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE stores normalized UTC and displays in session timezone; mapped to Snowflake TIMESTAMP_TZ. Review downstream session timezone assumptions.

tsql.review: T-SQL has no native INTERVAL type; manual redesign required.

mysql.review: MySQL has no INTERVAL column type; manual redesign required.

db2.review: DB2 INTERVAL handling varies; manual review required.

hana.review: HANA has no INTERVAL column type; manual review required.

snowflake.review: Oracle INTERVAL data type mapped to Snowflake INTERVAL. Review usage as Snowflake column data type support for INTERVAL may be limited; consider storing as numeric seconds/days or VARCHAR.

tsql.review: T-SQL has no native INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND type; manual redesign required.

mysql.review: MySQL has no INTERVAL column type.

db2.review: DB2 INTERVAL handling varies; manual review required.

hana.review: HANA has no INTERVAL column type.

snowflake.review: Oracle INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND mapped to Snowflake INTERVAL. Review usage as Snowflake column data type support for INTERVAL may be limited; consider storing as numeric seconds or VARCHAR.

tsql.review: T-SQL has no native INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH type; manual redesign required.

mysql.review: MySQL has no INTERVAL column type.

db2.review: DB2 INTERVAL handling varies; manual review required.

hana.review: HANA has no INTERVAL column type.

snowflake.review: Oracle INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH mapped to Snowflake INTERVAL. Review usage as Snowflake column data type support for INTERVAL may be limited; consider storing as numeric months or VARCHAR.

tsql.review: SMALLDECIMAL is HANA-specific; mapped to DECIMAL.

snowflake.review: SAP HANA SMALLDECIMAL is a floating-point decimal with variable scale; mapped to Snowflake NUMBER. Manual review recommended to confirm precision and scale requirements.
Oracle BINARY_FLOAT (32-bit IEEE float) mapped to Snowflake FLOAT.
Oracle BINARY_DOUBLE (64-bit IEEE double) mapped to Snowflake DOUBLE.

tsql.review: REAL is 32-bit; precision may differ across databases.

snowflake.review: REAL (32-bit single precision) mapped to Snowflake FLOAT (64-bit double precision).

tsql.review: T-SQL has no SERIAL; map to INTEGER and add identity handling separately.

mysql.review: MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is preferred; SERIAL maps to INTEGER with AUTO_INCREMENT behavior.

oracle.review: Oracle uses sequences; SERIAL mapped to NUMBER.

postgresql.review: Postgres SERIAL should be converted to AUTOINCREMENT or sequence; map to INTEGER for target and add identity handling.

snowflake.review: SERIAL is sequence-backed; convert to AUTOINCREMENT or recreate sequence+default in Snowflake.

postgresql.review: SMALLSERIAL should be converted to SMALLINT + autoincrement semantics.

snowflake.review: Convert to AUTOINCREMENT on Snowflake if needed.

postgresql.review: BIGSERIAL should be converted to BIGINT + autoincrement semantics.

snowflake.review: Convert to AUTOINCREMENT on Snowflake if needed.

tsql.review: SQL Server has no native ARRAY type.

mysql.review: MySQL does not use ARRAY as a column type.

oracle.review: Oracle nested tables / varrays require manual mapping.

postgresql.review: Array semantics differ; review element type mapping.

db2.review: DB2 array support differs; manual review.

hana.review: HANA array-like types require manual handling.

snowflake.review: Snowflake supports ARRAY; verify element types.

tsql.review: MONEY is SQL Server-specific; convert to DECIMAL/NUMBER with fixed precision.
DECFLOAT specific to DB2; manual review needed.

db2.review: DB2 DECFLOAT requires review; map to NUMBER or FLOAT depending on precision requirements.

snowflake.review: Map DECFLOAT to NUMBER by default; verify precision/behavior.

tsql.review: ROWID-like columns should be reviewed.

db2.review: DB2 ROWID mapping to VARCHAR; review usage.

snowflake.review: ROWID mapped to VARCHAR; verify uniqueness and format across platforms.

tsql.review: UROWID mapped to VARCHAR.

snowflake.review: Oracle UROWID (universal rowid for index-organized tables) mapped to Snowflake VARCHAR. Manual review required.

tsql.review: Implement GUID generation manually.

postgresql.review: PostgreSQL has native UUID type; consider using uuid-ossp extension.

tsql.review: XML must be handled differently in target database.

mysql.review: MySQL stores XML as text; no native XML type.

postgresql.review: PostgreSQL XML -> VARCHAR mapping; manual review required.

snowflake.review: Snowflake uses VARIANT for semi-structured data; XML may be stored as text or VARIANT after conversion.

tsql.review: XML must be handled differently in target database.

mysql.review: MySQL stores XML as text; no native XML type.

postgresql.review: PostgreSQL XML -> VARCHAR mapping; manual review required.

snowflake.review: Oracle XMLTYPE mapped to Snowflake VARIANT (or VARCHAR). XML data can be parsed into VARIANT or stored as VARCHAR text. Manual review required.

tsql.review: SQL_VARIANT is SQL Server-specific; convert to VARIANT or appropriate type.

mysql.review: MySQL JSON type for variant data.

oracle.review: Oracle lacks direct equivalent; use XMLTYPE or CLOB.

tsql.review: GEOGRAPHY semantics differ across databases.

oracle.review: Oracle uses SDO_GEOMETRY for spatial data.

snowflake.review: Snowflake GEOGRAPHY uses WGS84/GeoJSON.

tsql.review: Planar spatial type.

oracle.review: Oracle uses SDO_GEOMETRY for spatial data.

snowflake.review: Snowflake GEOMETRY uses planar spatial coordinates.

tsql.review: Spatial point type.

snowflake.review: SAP HANA ST_POINT mapped to Snowflake GEOGRAPHY (or GEOMETRY). Manual review required to verify coordinate system (WGS84 vs planar) and spatial operations.

tsql.review: Spatial geometry type.

snowflake.review: SAP HANA ST_GEOMETRY mapped to Snowflake GEOMETRY (or GEOGRAPHY). Manual review required to verify coordinate system / SRID and spatial functions.

tsql.review: HIERARCHYID has no equivalent; re-model as materialized path or adjacency list.

snowflake.review: HIERARCHYID has no equivalent; re-model.

tsql.review: ROWVERSION (row-version stamp) has no cross-database equivalent; use manual timestamps or CDC.

mysql.review: ROWVERSION has no equivalent; use TIMESTAMP or triggers.

oracle.review: ROWVERSION has no equivalent; use triggers or SCN tracking.

postgresql.review: ROWVERSION has no equivalent; use xmin or triggers.

db2.review: ROWVERSION has no equivalent; use ROWID or manual tracking.

hana.review: ROWVERSION has no equivalent; use manual tracking.

snowflake.review: ROWVERSION has no equivalent; use STREAMS or manual tracking.

function_mappings._comment: Dialect-specific function mappings for DEFAULT expressions and other contexts.

tsql.review: Ensure timezone handling is consistent.

snowflake.review: Verify session timezone.

tsql.review: GUID generation algorithm differs.

oracle.review: Oracle lacks native GUID; use UUID package or sequence.

oracle.template: -- Oracle: Use CREATE SEQUENCE seq_name START WITH {seed} INCREMENT BY {increment};

db2.template: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY (START WITH {seed} INCREMENT BY {increment})

constraint_notes.check: CHECK constraint syntax accepted but enforcement varies by database. Verify data integrity enforcement in application/ETL layer.
constraint_notes.foreign_key: FOREIGN KEY syntax accepted by most databases but enforcement varies. Application-level referential integrity may be required.
constraint_notes.primary_key: PRIMARY KEY syntax accepted universally but some databases (Snowflake) do not enforce. Verify uniqueness enforcement if critical.
constraint_notes.unique: UNIQUE constraint syntax accepted but enforcement varies. Test behavior in target database.
